Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **The quick menu along the bottom of the message window**: inside the window at both sizes (at the larger size phones start with it ran past the window's end), with icons for moving through the story, the history, a screenshot and Config, and the saves still in words; the window's text keeps four lines above it
- **Swipes no longer go on to the next text**: KAG clicks as a finger touches, so a swipe had already moved the text on; on a touch screen the touch now waits for the finger to lift (a tap goes on, a swipe runs its action), and in a browser the game now gets touches at all
- **The quick menu's pin works on phones**, and the Effects demo's static draws over the quick menu
- **Panels on the quick menu's buttons**: a right-click, a long press, or (as Config says) the pointer resting on Config, Auto or Q.LOAD opens the volumes, the text's settings or the newest quick saves over the scene
- **A long press** on the story runs an action of its own (the sample's: auto mode) and shows a button's tip; **the mouse's back and forward buttons** go back a line and on; Change Controls orders the quick menu's buttons
- **Help lines**: Config, the save screens and Extras say at their bottom what the pointer is on, and every setting has a line of help as its tip
- **Extras scroll**: the CG and Replay tiles are grids and the music room's tracks a list that scroll with the wheel, dragging and flicks
- **Cards** with the picture after a quick save or a screenshot; skipping says that it started and why it stopped; Config's Movie Volume plays a sample; Reduce Motion's still pictures and animations change at once as it's turned on or off
- kagex-release 0.20.0 downloads the 0.20.0 engines

The sample game with Live2D (`kagex_sample_live2d_<platform>`, added to this release once it's out) holds Live2D's Cubism Core: by installing or playing it you agree not to copy the Cubism Core out of it, distribute it apart from the game, modify it, or reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble it. It uses sample data owned and copyrighted by Live2D Inc.

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.20.0/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tools aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tools, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release kagex-lipsync`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
